correctness.rationale: A Euclidean diametral endpoint of any polytope must be a vertex by strict convexity of the Euclidean norm. The actual source Proposition 2.7 says each k-support vertex uses labels n,n-1,...,n-k+1. For nonnegative coordinates, (u_i-v_i)^2 = u_i^2+v_i^2-2u_iv_i <= max(u_i^2,v_i^2), strict when both are positive. Summation selects at most m of the doubled strictly ordered square labels; the maximal m entries are split evenly into two possible prefix lengths, and disjoint supports realize them. Equality forces no overlap and exactly those labels. Checked m,n=(2,3),(3,2),(4,3),(5,3),(6,2) by independently enumerated vertex pairs, with matching squared diameters 18,9,26,27,10. These finite cases corroborate, not prove, the all-parameter bound. Domain n,m positive including m=1 and saturation m>=2n.

value.rationale: A complete Euclidean-diameter formula and equality classification for a named natural two-parameter family of anti-blocking permutation polytopes fills an exact metric invariant gap. The sharp ambient dimension threshold m=2n is a structural phenomenon, not an arbitrary numeric slice; it differs essentially from inradius and minimum enclosing radius.

limitations: Standard ambient Euclidean metric and vertices of the designated P(m,n), not graph diameter or generalized permutohedra.
No assertion about circumradius, John/Löwner ellipsoids, or arbitrary norms.
